```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr); library(leaflet); library(DT); library(htmltools)
})
source("R/panels.R")   # shared palettes, theme and plot builders

bh  <- read_csv("data/bethel_boreholes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(across(c(permafrost, talik, visible_ice, massive_ice),
                ~factor(.x, levels = c("Yes", "No"))))

dtm_w    <- rast("data/msgc_dtm_1m_web.tif")
relief_w <- rast("data/msgc_relief_1m_web.tif")
hs_w     <- rast("data/msgc_hillshade_1m_web.tif")
slope_w  <- rast("data/msgc_slope_1m_web.tif")
foot     <- st_read("data/msgc_footprint.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)

pal_yn <- colorFactor(c(YES_COL, NO_COL), levels = c("Yes", "No"))

# --- headline numbers, all computed from the data --------------------------
n_bh        <- nrow(bh)
n_reports   <- dplyr::n_distinct(bh$report)
yr_rng      <- range(bh$report_year, na.rm = TRUE)
drill_rng   <- range(bh$drill_year,  na.rm = TRUE)
n_pf        <- sum(bh$permafrost  == "Yes")
n_talik     <- sum(bh$talik       == "Yes")
n_vis       <- sum(bh$visible_ice == "Yes")
n_massive   <- sum(bh$massive_ice == "Yes")
pf_top_med  <- median(bh$pf_top_m, na.rm = TRUE)
foot_ha     <- as.numeric(st_area(st_transform(foot, 32606))) / 1e4
relief_vals <- values(relief_w, na.rm = TRUE)
pct_low     <- mean(relief_vals < -0.5) * 100

# transect across the most pronounced closed hollow, shared by map and profile
prof      <- pick_profile(dtm_w, relief_w, slope_w)
hollow_m  <- abs(min(prof$rel))
prof_line <- st_sfc(st_linestring(cbind(range(prof$x),
                                        rep(attr(prof, "centre")[2], 2))),
                    crs = 3857) |> st_transform(4326)
```

#  Overview

## Row {height="18%"}

::: {.card title="Researchers and farmers working together to understand permafrost-agriculture interactions"}
Permafrost Grown works with farmers in Alaska to understand how permafrost and
agricultural activities interact. The goal is to develop management strategies and
best-practice guides for farmers cultivating on permafrost-affected soils. In
**year three of five**, the team has collected a wide range of data on the physical,
social, economic and policy impacts of permafrost on northern farms.

This dashboard presents the Year 3 highlights with the underlying data made
explorable - pan, zoom, switch layers and search the records yourself.
:::

## Row {height="62%"}

### Column {width="55%"}

```{r}
#| title: "Where the Year 3 work happened"
sites <- data.frame(
  name = c("Midnight Sun Golf Course, Fairbanks", "Bethel, Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta"),
  lab  = c("Drone lidar monitoring of thaw subsidence on a legacy farm field",
           "Synthesis of borehole records and discovery of ice wedges"),
  lon  = c(mean(st_bbox(foot)[c("xmin","xmax")]), mean(bh$lon)),
  lat  = c(mean(st_bbox(foot)[c("ymin","ymax")]), mean(bh$lat)))

leaflet(sites, options = leafletOptions(minZoom = 3)) |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldTopoMap") |>
  addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 9, color = "#1b5e4b", weight = 2,
                   fillColor = "#c9892b", fillOpacity = .9,
                   label = ~name,
                   popup = ~paste0("<b>", name, "</b><br>", lab)) |>
  setView(lng = -153, lat = 63.3, zoom = 4) |>
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft")
```

### Column {width="45%"}

::: {.card title="What is on this dashboard"}
::: {.lead-note}
**Using drones to monitor thaw subsidence** - 3D digital surface models let the team
track how much the land has lowered as ground ice melts. Up to **1.5 m (about 5 feet)**
of thaw subsidence occurred between 2017 and 2023 at a site first cleared for
agriculture and cultivated until it was abandoned and converted into a golf course.
Permafrost can keep degrading, with active thaw subsidence, long after cultivation stops.
:::

::: {.lead-note}
**Discovery of ice wedges in the Bethel area** - near-surface permafrost information
was synthesised from archived geotechnical reports, together with boreholes the team
drilled in 2023 and 2024. That drilling found **wedge ice**, a type of massive ground
ice not previously described in the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta.
:::

::: {.lead-note}
**Engaging farmers** - interviews, on-farm engagement, annual surveys, focus groups
and workshops bring farmers and researchers together to generate new knowledge about
permafrost-agroecosystems.
:::
:::

#  Thaw subsidence

## Row {height="8%"}

::: {.card}
**Using drones to monitor thaw subsidence - Midnight Sun Golf Course, Fairbanks.**
A 65 ha parcel cleared for agriculture, cultivated until it was abandoned, and converted
to a golf course about 25 years ago. Ice-rich permafrost thaw following the original
clearing contributed to that change in land use.
:::

## Row {height="62%"}

```{r}
#| title: "2023 drone lidar - ground surface and thaw features"
ext_ll <- st_bbox(foot)

hs_pal  <- colorNumeric(grey.colors(64, start = .15, end = .97), domain = NULL,
                        na.color = "transparent")
rel_rng <- c(-1.5, 1.5)
rel_clamped <- clamp(relief_w, rel_rng[1], rel_rng[2], values = TRUE)
rel_pal <- colorNumeric(
  colorRampPalette(c("#67001f", "#d6604d", "#f7f7f7", "#92c5de", "#2166ac"))(64),
  domain = rel_rng, na.color = "transparent", reverse = TRUE)
elev_pal <- colorNumeric(terrain.colors(64, rev = TRUE), domain = NULL,
                         na.color = "transparent")

leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satellite image") |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldTopoMap",  group = "Topographic map") |>
  addRasterImage(hs_w, colors = hs_pal, opacity = 1, project = FALSE,
                 group = "Shaded relief (2023)") |>
  addRasterImage(rel_clamped, colors = rel_pal, opacity = .72, project = FALSE,
                 group = "Low ground / thaw features") |>
  addRasterImage(dtm_w, colors = elev_pal, opacity = .7, project = FALSE,
                 group = "Ground elevation") |>
  addPolygons(data = foot, fill = FALSE, color = "#7a5a18", weight = 1.5,
              dashArray = "4 4", group = "Drone survey coverage") |>
  addPolylines(data = prof_line, color = "#c9892b", weight = 4, opacity = .95,
               group = "Profile line",
               label = "Ground profile shown below") |>
  addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = rel_pal, values = rel_rng,
            opacity = .8, title = "Height relative to<br>surrounding ground (m)",
            labFormat = labelFormat(suffix = " m")) |>
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups    = c("Satellite image", "Topographic map"),
    overlayGroups = c("Shaded relief (2023)", "Low ground / thaw features",
                      "Ground elevation", "Drone survey coverage",
                      "Profile line"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) |>
  hideGroup("Ground elevation") |>
  fitBounds(ext_ll[["xmin"]], ext_ll[["ymin"]], ext_ll[["xmax"]], ext_ll[["ymax"]]) |>
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft")
```

::: {.source-note}
Source: Midnight Sun Golf Course classified lidar point cloud, digital surface model,
digital terrain model and orthophoto mosaic, 10 September 2023
([doi:10.18739/A2W37KX40](https://doi.org/10.18739/A2W37KX40)).
Shaded relief and the "low ground" layer are derived here from the published 2023
digital terrain model; blue tones mark ground sitting below the local average surface -
the pits, troughs and collapsed hollows that thawing ground ice leaves behind.
The 2017-2023 change map in the printed Year 3 highlights uses an earlier borough lidar
survey that is not part of this dataset and is not reproduced here.
:::

#  Bethel ice wedges

## Row {height="8%"}

::: {.card}
**Discovery of ice wedges in the Bethel area.** Bethel sits in a zone of discontinuous
permafrost and was thought to lack ice wedges. To investigate the agricultural potential
of the area, the team synthesised near-surface permafrost information from archived
geotechnical reports, alongside boreholes drilled in 2023 and 2024. That drilling found
wedge ice - a type of massive ground ice not previously described in the
Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta.
:::

## Row {height="72%"}

### Column {width="58%"}

```{r}
#| title: "Near-surface permafrost from Bethel geotechnical boreholes"
popup_txt <- paste0(
  "<b>", bh$site_id, "</b><br>",
  "Borehole: ", bh$borehole_id, "<br>",
  "Report: ", bh$report, " (", bh$report_year, ")<br>",
  "Drilled: ", ifelse(is.na(bh$drill_date), "not recorded",
                      format(bh$drill_date)), "<br>",
  "Borehole depth: ", sprintf("%.1f m", bh$depth_m), "<br>",
  "Depth to frozen ground: ",
  ifelse(is.na(bh$pf_top_m), "not reported", sprintf("%.1f m", bh$pf_top_m)), "<br>",
  "<hr style='margin:4px 0'>",
  "Permafrost: <b>", bh$permafrost, "</b> &nbsp; Talik: <b>", bh$talik, "</b><br>",
  "Visible ice: <b>", bh$visible_ice, "</b> &nbsp; Massive ice: <b>",
  bh$massive_ice, "</b>")

m <- leaflet(bh) |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satellite image") |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldTopoMap", group = "Topographic map")

layers <- list("Permafrost present"    = "permafrost",
               "Talik (unfrozen zone)" = "talik",
               "Visible ground ice"    = "visible_ice",
               "Massive ground ice"    = "massive_ice")

for (nm in names(layers)) {
  v <- bh[[layers[[nm]]]]
  m <- addCircleMarkers(m, lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat, group = nm,
                        radius = 4.5, stroke = TRUE, weight = 1, color = "#2b2b2b",
                        fillColor = pal_yn(v), fillOpacity = .9,
                        label = ~site_id, popup = popup_txt)
}

m |>
  addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal_yn, values = c("Yes", "No"),
            title = "Reported in<br>borehole log", opacity = .9) |>
  addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Satellite image", "Topographic map"),
                   overlayGroups = names(layers),
                   options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) |>
  hideGroup(setdiff(names(layers), "Permafrost present")) |>
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft")
```

::: {.source-note}
Source: Synthesis of near-surface permafrost borehole information from Bethel
geotechnical reports ([doi:10.18739/A2P55DJ80](https://doi.org/10.18739/A2P55DJ80)).
Tick one indicator at a time in the layer box; click any borehole for its full record.
:::

::: {.so-what}
**Why ice wedges matter** - wedge ice is a body of nearly pure ice in the ground. When it
thaws, the surface above it collapses into troughs and ponds rather than settling evenly.
Knowing where it occurs changes where you would site a building pad, a road, a utility
run or a field.
:::

#  The borehole records

## Row

```{r}
#| title: "All Bethel borehole records - search, sort and download"
tbl <- bh |>
  transmute(`Site ID` = site_id,
            Borehole = borehole_id,
            Agency = agency,
            Report = report,
            `Report year` = report_year,
            Drilled = drill_date,
            `Depth (m)` = round(depth_m, 1),
            `Depth to frozen ground (m)` = round(pf_top_m, 1),
            `Base of frozen ground not reached` =
              ifelse(pf_base_not_reached, "yes", ""),
            Permafrost = permafrost, Talik = talik,
            `Visible ice` = visible_ice, `Massive ice` = massive_ice,
            Latitude = round(lat, 5), Longitude = round(lon, 5))

datatable(tbl, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
          extensions = c("Buttons", "Scroller"),
          options = list(dom = "Bfrtip", buttons = c("csv", "excel"),
                         deferRender = TRUE, scrollY = 460, scroller = TRUE,
                         scrollX = TRUE)) |>
  formatStyle("Permafrost",
              backgroundColor = styleEqual(c("Yes", "No"), c("#dbeaf5", "#f5f5f5"))) |>
  formatStyle("Massive ice",
              backgroundColor = styleEqual(c("Yes", "No"), c("#f9d9b8", "#f5f5f5")))
```

::: {.source-note}
"Base of frozen ground not reached" marks logs where the driller was still in frozen
ground at the bottom of the hole, so the permafrost is at least as thick as the hole is
deep. Blank depth cells are records where the original report gave no value.
:::

#  Working with farmers

## Row {height="55%"}

### Column {width="52%"}

::: {.card title="Engaging farmers to understand impacts"}
The research team has collaborated with farmers to understand their experiences of
farming within a permafrost-agroecosystem (PAE) through:

- interviews
- on-farm engagement
- annual surveys
- focus groups
- workshops

Together, farmers and researchers generate new knowledge and identify knowledge gaps
through activities like a **Permafrost Degradation Game** and a
**Land-purchasing Scenario Exercise**. These activities have highlighted increasing
awareness of the need to understand the complex nature of a permafrost-agroecosystem's
biophysical properties for informed farm management.

The collaboration explores the social and ecological dimensions of agricultural
management, providing guidance for mitigation, adaptive strategies and policy
recommendations.
:::

### Column {width="48%"}

::: {.card title="Putting it to work"}
::: {.so-what}
**Before you clear land** - ice content below the surface, not the vegetation on top,
decides how the ground will behave afterwards. A few boreholes or a ground-penetrating
radar line is far cheaper than regrading a settled field.
:::
::: {.so-what}
**After clearing** - settling continues for years. Plan drainage for a surface that will
keep changing shape, and re-survey periodically rather than once.
:::
::: {.so-what}
**For local government** - the same measurements that help a farm plan a field help a
borough plan a road alignment, a gravel pad or a utility corridor. Both datasets behind
this dashboard are openly licensed and can be loaded straight into GIS software.
:::
:::

#  Data & methods

## Row

### Column

::: {.card title="Where the data comes from"}
**Midnight Sun Golf Course drone lidar, Fairbanks.**
Midnight Sun Golf Course Classified LiDAR Point Cloud, Digital Surface Model, Digital
Terrain Model, Digital Photos, and Orthophoto Mosaic, 10 September 2023.
Arctic Data Center, [doi:10.18739/A2W37KX40](https://doi.org/10.18739/A2W37KX40).
Acquired with a DJI M300 drone carrying a Zenmuse L1 sensor flown in RTK mode at 60 m
above ground level; the point cloud was classified into ground and non-ground returns and
gridded to 25 cm digital surface and terrain models in WGS84 UTM Zone 6N, ellipsoid
heights.

**Bethel borehole synthesis, Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta.**
Synthesis of near-surface permafrost borehole information from Bethel geotechnical
reports. Arctic Data Center,
[doi:10.18739/A2P55DJ80](https://doi.org/10.18739/A2P55DJ80).
Historical geotechnical drilling reports were scanned, made searchable with OCR, and the
borehole records - depth to permafrost, permafrost presence, visible ice, massive ice and
borehole depth - extracted by hand into a spatial table.
:::

### Column

::: {.card title="How the layers on this dashboard were made"}
```{r}
notes <- data.frame(
  Layer = c("Shaded relief (2023)",
            "Low ground / thaw features",
            "Ground elevation",
            "Borehole points",
            "Depth to frozen ground"),
  `How it was derived` = c(
    "Hillshade of the published 25 cm terrain model, averaged to a 1 m grid (sun 35 degrees altitude, 315 degrees azimuth).",
    "Terrain model minus its own 61 m moving average. Negative values are ground lying below the local average surface.",
    "Published 25 cm terrain model averaged to a 1 m grid; ellipsoid heights in metres.",
    "Published borehole table, plotted at its recorded latitude and longitude.",
    "Field Frozen_Ground_Depth_Top, with the value 999 treated as missing per the dataset's metadata."),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(notes)
```

::: {.source-note}
The printed Year 3 highlights show a 2017-2023 elevation-difference map built by
differencing borough lidar flown in 2017 against the 2023 drone survey. The 2017 survey
is not part of the published dataset, so this dashboard shows the 2023 surface and its
thaw features directly rather than recomputing the change map. The 1.5 m figure quoted
throughout is the project's own published result.

Record counts: the borehole table holds `r n_bh` records naming `r n_reports` distinct
reports, with report years `r yr_rng[1]`-`r yr_rng[2]` and drilling dates
`r drill_rng[1]`-`r drill_rng[2]`. The archived dataset also includes the scanned source
reports. Massive ice is flagged in `r n_massive` of these historical records; the wedge
ice described in the Year 3 highlights was found in the team's own 2023-2024 drilling,
which is reported separately.
:::
:::
